newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 28.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.
- Britain's Tony Blair warns Sinn Fein that its campaign of terror will make its entry into the political process "all the more difficult.
- Decision day for former prime minister Charles Haughey as his solicitor Noel Smyth takes the stand for the second time at a tribunal in Dublin castle.
- Both sides in the paramedics dispute are to give submissions to the Labour court today.
- Uncertain times for Mackie International who recently said it may restate it accounts.
- A scheme to restructure Bell Lines is being circulated to creditors and shareholders
- Dollar bills mount up as U2 brings Pop around the world
- Former minister Michael Lowry is facing an all-out battle for his political survival after further revelations about his private and business life.
- Justice minister Nora Owens unleashes attack on Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern.
- Haulage firms face 10 million punt loss in Bell Lines revamp
- The newly formed Development Companies Market of the Irish stock exchange has attracted its first public flotation
- Kingspan signs 50 million punt syndicated loan deal
